image_description: The screenshot shows the HWiNFO application, a system information and monitoring tool. The main window displays detailed hardware information in a tree view on the left, with specific details for components like the CPU, memory, and graphics card. A pop-up window in the center provides a more focused view of the Intel Core i7-4700MQ processor, including its clock speed, core count, and other specifications. On the right, a "Feature" panel lists general information about the CPU, such as its name, original frequency, and product unit. A small graph in the top right corner shows the current clock speed of the CPU. The application is running on a Windows 10 system.

The screenshot shows the Code::Blocks Integrated Development Environment (IDE). The main window displays a C++ source file named `terrain.cpp` in the editor, with syntax highlighting. The code includes function calls like `nFontManager->GetDefaultFont()` and `nCamera->SetUserCameraMovementControls(true)`. A section of code is highlighted in yellow, which appears to be a function call `mTerrain->load("heightmap.bsp")`. On the left, a project explorer pane shows a list of files within a project, including `game.cpp`, `main.cpp`, and other `.cpp` and `.h` files. The top menu bar includes options like File, Edit, View, Search, Project, Compile, Debug, Tools, and Help. Various toolbars are visible below the menu bar.

The screenshot displays the CrystalDiskInfo application, version 9.0.0 x64. The main focus is on a Samsung SSD 990 PRO 2TB drive, which is identified as Drive Letter S:. The health status of the drive is shown as "Good" with a 100% rating. The current temperature of the drive is 51°C. Key information for the selected drive includes: Firmware (1B2QJXD7), Serial Number (partially masked), Interface (NVM Express), Transfer Mode (PCIe 4.0 x4 | PCIe 4.0 x4), and features like S.M.A.R.T., TRIM, and VolatileWriteCache. A table at the bottom lists various S.M.A.R.T. attributes, such as Critical Warning, Composite Temperature, Available Spare, Percentage Used, and more, along with their raw values. The top of the window shows tabs for different drives, including Disk1 through Disk10, some of which also display temperatures.

The screenshot displays the graphical user interface of the "Boot Repair" application. The window has a dark gray title bar with the text "Boot Repair". Below this, the main content area has a light gray background. On the left side, there is a circular icon depicting a wrench and screwdriver over a blue globe-like shape. To the right of the icon, two buttons are presented: "Recommended repair (repairs most frequent problems)" which is highlighted with an orange border, and "Create a BootInfo summary (to get help by email or forum)". Below these options, there is a collapsible section labeled "Advanced options" with a small arrow indicating it can be expanded. At the bottom of the window, there are two buttons: "About" on the left and "Quit" on the right.

The screenshot displays the "Options" window of the KeePass password manager application. The "Interface (1)" tab is currently selected, showing various configuration settings. The main content area is divided into sections: "Start and Exit", "After Opening a Database", and "Auto-Type". Under "Start and Exit", several checkboxes are visible, including options to remember and open the last used database on startup, limit to a single instance, check for updates, start minimized or locked, and automatically save when closing or modifying an entry. The "Auto-Type" section has a checkbox for enabling auto-type functionality, with sub-options for matching entries based on title, URL, or tags in the target window title. At the bottom of the window, there are "OK" and "Cancel" buttons, and a search bar at the very bottom.

The screenshot shows the Apache OpenOffice application, specifically in its Math module. The main window displays a mathematical formula: f(x,y) = (e^M * sqrt(cos(x) + tan(y))) / M^2. On the right side, there is a panel labeled "Elements" with various mathematical symbols and functions like 'a', 'b', 'f(x)', 'Σ', 'sin', 'cos', etc., for building equations. At the bottom of the screen, a text box contains the LaTeX-like code for the displayed formula: f(x,y) = {func e^(M) cdot sqrt{cos(x) + tan(y) } } over {M^(2)}.

The screenshot shows the Dev-C++ integrated development environment (IDE) with a C++ project open. The main window displays a code editor with a file named "main.cpp" being edited. The code is written in C++ and contains functions, loops, and conditional statements, including `#ifdef PRINT` and `#endif` blocks. A function call to `SuggestHigherCard()` is highlighted, and a tooltip for this function is visible, showing its parameters. The left panel shows a project tree with files like "player.h", "HumanPlayer", and "jcmes.cpp". The top menu bar includes options like File, Edit, Search, and Project. The status bar at the bottom indicates the current line number, column, and other details.

The screenshot displays the qBittorrent application, version 4.6.4. The main window shows a list of torrents being downloaded or managed. There is one active transfer labeled "Ubuntu 22.04". The search bar at the top contains the query "Ubuntu 22.04". Below it, the results section shows 27 out of 28 entries matching the search. The columns displayed are Name, Size, Seeders, and Leechers. Various Ubuntu ISO files are listed, including server versions and different desktop packages like gnome and kde. The interface includes standard menu options (File, Edit, View, Tools, Help), toolbar icons for adding new torrents, pausing, starting, and deleting downloads, as well as tabs for Transfers, Search, RSS, and Execution Log.

The screenshot displays the user interface of the "Scrollout F1" application, which appears to be a network security or email filtering tool. The main window is dark-themed with a navigation bar at the top containing tabs like CONNECT, ROUTE, SECURE, COLLECT, and MONITOR. A dropdown menu from the "SECURE" tab is open, showing options such as LEVELS, SENDERS, COUNTRIES, CERTIFICATE, and PASSWORD. The central area features a table with columns labeled AGGRESSIVE, OPTIMUM, and PERMISSIVE, each with numbered levels from 1 to 10, some of which are marked with checkmarks. The top of the screen shows system metrics for network traffic, CPU, RAM, and disk usage. At the bottom, there are sections for "Check Sender Name Servers (Names)" and "Check Sender Name Servers (IPs)", with corresponding domain names listed.

The screenshot shows the Safe Exam Browser application in use. The main window displays a video titled "Test Video" which is paused at 0:00, showing a woman holding a sign that says "Media Player". Below the video player are playback controls and a section labeled "Bildunterschrift" (German for subtitle). A modal dialog box titled "Preferences" is open over the main window. This dialog contains fields for "Start URL", "Administrator password", "Confirm administrator password", "Allow user to quit SEB", "Quit password", and "Confirm quit password". The "Allow user to quit SEB" checkbox is checked. The dialog has buttons for "About", "Quit", "Cancel", "Restart", and "OK". The top bar of the application shows the title "Safe Exam Browser" and indicates the user is logged in as "Daniel Schneider".

The screenshot shows the XAMPP Control Panel v3.2.2 running on a Windows system. The main window lists several services: Apache, MySQL, FileZilla, Mercury, and Tomcat. Each service has a checkbox, a "Start" button, an "Admin" button, a "Config" button, and a "Logs" link. The log at the bottom of the window shows that the control panel is initializing, checking prerequisites, and starting modules. The "Apache" and "MySQL" services are not yet started, as indicated by the unchecked boxes. The "XAMPP Version" is 5.5.30, and the installation directory is "c:\xamppp5.6\".

The screenshot displays a terminal window with text output from the "Ubuntuzilla" application. The title bar confirms the application name as "Ubuntuzilla: Mozilla Software Installer". The terminal shows that it has detected Firefox version 2.0.0.6 and is prompting the user to confirm if this version should be installed by typing 'y' or 'n'. Following this, it begins retrieving a list of available localizations for Firefox and presents a numbered menu from 0 to 43, listing various language codes such as 'af', 'ar', 'bg', etc., instructing the user to choose one.

The screenshot shows the Acrylic DNS Proxy UI window, which is a configuration tool for a DNS proxy service. The main content area displays a text file, which appears to be a configuration file named "AcrylicConfiguration.ini". The file contains various settings in a key-value format, with comments explaining each setting. Visible sections include [GlobalSection] and options such as PrimaryServerAddress (set to 8.8.8.8), PrimaryServerPort (set to 53), and PrimaryServerProtocol (set to UDP). The status bar at the bottom indicates that the user is currently editing this file.

The screenshot displays the AGATHA Legacy media player application. The main interface is dark with a central logo of a white bird holding a blue musical note. On the right side, there is a playlist titled "Buscar en la Lista..." which lists 15 tracks by AC/DC from their album "Black Ice [2008]". The currently playing track is highlighted as "01 AC-DC - Rock N Roll Train.mp3". At the bottom of the screen, a playback control bar shows that the song has started at 0:12 out of a total duration of 4:08.

The screenshot displays the graphical user interface of the AdvTor application, version 0.3.0.12. A modal dialog box titled "Generate an .onion address" is in the foreground, prompting the user to create a new hidden service address. The dialog shows a text field with the prefix "test" and a list of generated addresses below it, with the first one being "leszcz5bm5fkoesj.onion". The main window behind the dialog has various configuration options for a Tor proxy, including fields for real port, real address, virtual port, and onion address. The left sidebar contains a navigation menu with options like Proxy, Banned addresses, HTTP headers, and System. At the bottom of the main window, there are several buttons: Connect, New identity, Save settings, Always on top, Minimize to tray, and Exit.

The screenshot shows a software application window titled "AIM Toolkit". The main content of the window is a dialog box for "Mount New Virtual Disk". This dialog contains several input fields and options. At the top, there is a text field labeled "Image File:" with a button to browse for a file. Below this, there are two radio button groups. The first group allows the user to select between "Drive Letter" (selected) and "Mount Point", with a dropdown menu for the drive letter set to "Auto". The second group allows the user to select the "Device Type", with "Hard Disk" selected. There are also checkboxes for "Read-only", "Removable", and "Mount at Windows Startup". At the bottom of the dialog, there are "OK" and "Cancel" buttons.

The screenshot shows a software interface with a dark theme, likely for a game. The main content is divided into three columns. The leftmost column contains navigation tabs labeled "AIMBOT", "VISUALS", "MISC", and "SETTINGS". The central column displays settings for the "AIMBOT" feature, including options like "Aimbot Enabled", "Aim Key" (set to Left), "Always Aim", "Sensitivity" (100%), and "Reaction Time" (0ms). The rightmost column, under the "PREDICTIONS" section, has a toggle for "Predict" which is turned on. The top of the screen shows the title "AimAhead" and the bottom right corner displays the current frames per second (FPS) as 185.

The screenshot shows the user interface of an application named "AIMr". The main content area displays a changelog for version 2.3, which includes additions like Mousebuttons, new aim calculations, an Always-on option, tooltips, and more. Below the changelog, there is a message about potential configuration issues. A prominent button labeled "Join the discord!" with a Discord logo is visible. At the bottom, a User ID and copyright information are displayed. The top of the window has a navigation bar with tabs: FAQ, Presets, General, Aimbot, and Triggerbot. A purple button at the very top says "Start AI Aimbot".

The screenshot shows a terminal window with a black background and white text. The title bar of the window indicates the process name is "airgeddon.mirror" and the title is "airgeddon". The main content of the screen displays the "airgeddon" script version 11.0, with a large, stylized logo in yellow text. Below the logo, it says "Developed by visitor" in green. A small, simple graphic of a flying saucer is visible at the bottom. The user is logged in as 'root' on a system named 'vis10r', and the current directory is the home directory.

The screenshot shows the AkelPad text editor application. The window title bar displays "AkelPad - [c:\akelpad_4\AkelPad.cpp]". The main editing area contains C/C++ source code with various include directives such as <windows.h>, <commdlg.h>, and <shellapi.h>. There are also several preprocessor directives like #define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN and #define AEC_FUNCTIONS. At the bottom of the screen, there is a status bar showing information about the current file: "AkelHistory-Rus.txt", "AkelPad.cpp", line number 4:15, column 10, mode "Ins", language "Win", and character encoding "1251 (ANSI - кириллица)".

The screenshot shows a software application window titled "File Browser". The main content area displays a list of audio files with columns for Artist, Album, and Artwork Status. The artist listed is "Muse" for all entries, and the albums are "Showbiz", "Origin Of Symmetry", "Black Holes And Revelations", "B-Sides", and "Absolution". The "Artwork Status" column indicates that all albums except the last one have "Not Present" artwork, while the "Absolution" album has a checkmark next to "Found: Folder.jpg". At the bottom of the window, it states "0 of 5 albums selected" and there is a button labeled "Get Artwork for Selection...".

The screenshot shows a software application window titled "LF Aligner". The main content is a dialog box with the heading "Please provide the settings for the TMX". It contains several input fields: "TMX language code for English" set to "EN-GB", "TMX language code for Hungarian" set to "HU", a checkbox labeled "Note to be added to each TU" which is checked, and fields for "Creator ID" and "Creation date" with values "LF Aligner 3.0" and "20120603T093334Z" respectively. A note at the bottom provides guidance on using language codes in TMX files. A "Next" button is visible in the lower right corner of the dialog.

The screenshot displays a software testing report interface titled "Allure report / 10 September 2023". The main focus is a donut chart showing the test results: 45.86% passed, 33% failed, 16% broken, 6% skipped, and 6% unknown. A total of 8901 test cases are shown. To the right, a stacked area chart labeled "Trend" visualizes the test status over time, with a legend for Failed (red), Broken (yellow), Passed (green), Skipped (gray), and Unknown (purple). Below, a list of "Suites" shows 9 items, with their names and a count of 1 in red (Failed) and yellow (Broken) for some.

The screenshot displays a web-based utility titled "Disk Wizard". At the top, there are navigation tabs labeled Logout, Status, Setup, Disk, Services, and Packages. The main content area shows two detected disks: one labeled 'right' with an sda device and 80.0 GB capacity, and another labeled 'left' with an sdb device and 82.3 GB capacity. Below this, there is a section titled "Whirl your magic wand..." which presents radio buttons for selecting disk configuration options such as "Don't touch my disks in any way!", "One big filesystem per disk", and various RAID configurations. Further down, another set of radio buttons allows selection of filesystem types including ext2, ext3, and ext4. At the bottom left corner, there is a button labeled "Abracadabra". The cursor is positioned over the "Abra" portion of the button.

The image shows a smartphone screen with a dark interface. The main display area has a large, circular button in the center with the text "Connected" inside. Below this, there is a message indicating "Split tunneling enabled" with a dropdown arrow. At the bottom of the screen, a section labeled "My Server" is visible, with a dropdown menu and the text "Amnezia DNS | XRay" underneath. The phone is being held by a hand, and the background is dark with blue and red lighting on the edges of the device.

The screenshot shows a software application, Notepad++, with a file named "LICENSE" open. The file content is the GNU General Public License (GPL). A plugin called "Analyse Plugin" is active, and its window is open on the right side of the screen. This plugin is performing a search within the text, as indicated by the "Search" field, "Case" and "Whole word" options, and a list of "Analyse Result" entries in a table format. The results show that the term "GPl" was found 64 times, and the first result is highlighted. The main text editor area also has a line of text selected.

The screenshot displays the Amarok Linux desktop environment. A terminal window titled "Amarok Terminal -" is open in the center of the screen. The terminal shows a welcome message for "Amarok Linux 2.1 jean," followed by system information including the date and time (segunda 26 outubro 2020, 11:32:40), memory usage (511/3941MB), and disk usage (5/20GB). It also provides links to the website and support forums. The prompt at the bottom indicates the user is logged in as 'jean'. The desktop background features the Amarok Linux logo. On the left side, there are icons for "Lixeira", "Sistema...", and "Início". The taskbar at the bottom contains several application icons.

The screenshot shows a game interface, likely a strategy or simulation game, with a top-down view of a colorful, procedurally generated world. The terrain is composed of various biomes, represented by different colors such as green, blue, orange, and purple, with rivers and other geographical features. Numerous small icons are scattered across the map, representing in-game entities like buildings, resources, or characters. In the top-left corner, text displays "Numeric Seed: 24922" and "World Type: Default". A label for an entity named "Igloo" is visible with coordinates [1800, 232]. The bottom left shows the frame rate (FPS) at 50.0, and a scale bar indicates "1000 blocks". The overall aesthetic is pixelated.

The screenshot shows a desktop environment with a train station as the background wallpaper. In the top right corner, there is a system monitor widget displaying information such as the operating system (antiX), date and time, uptime, network status, CPU usage, disk usage, and battery level. On the left side of the screen, there are two application icons: one for a file manager and another for a terminal. The bottom of the screen features a taskbar with a menu button, a workspace switcher, and a clock showing 12:18.

The screenshot shows a terminal window with a command-line interface. The title of the application is "Annie". The command executed is `annie -l https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ`, which is used to list the available video streams for a YouTube link. The output displays information about the video, including its title ("Rick Astley - NEVER GONNA GIVE YOU UP (Video)"), type, and a list of available quality options. Each option includes details like quality (e.g., 1080p, 720p), file format, codec, and size. The user is presented with different download options, such as 1080p, 720p, and 480p, each with a corresponding command to download the stream.

The screenshot shows the Apache NetBeans integrated development environment (IDE). The main area displays a Java file with a `main` method. A code completion dropdown is open, showing suggestions for the variable name "i" and other options like "args", "firstNumber", and "secondNumber". The user has typed "i" and the IDE is offering a list of possible completions, which include variables from the current scope and class members. The text below the code provides instructions on how to use the code completion feature, specifically mentioning that pressing Ctrl + Space a second time will show all available items.

The screenshot displays the AnyTXT Searcher 1.2 Free application window. The interface includes a menu bar at the top with options like File, Edit, View, and Tools. A dropdown menu from the "Tools" option is open, showing various tools such as Fuzzy Match, Whole Match, Index Manager, Language, Translate, System Tray, and Context Menu. On the left side of the screen, there's a list of files under the "file names" section. In the main area, there's a table detailing file suffixes and their descriptions, including formats like .xls, .pptx, .pdf, and others. Below this table, text explains how to search for specific file types using the software. At the bottom of the window, a status bar indicates that 8 files were found in 0.582 seconds, and the search is complete. The user is currently on page 5 of 6.

The screenshot shows a code editor with a JavaScript file named "index.js". The code is written in a syntax that appears to be for an Apollo Client GraphQL query. It defines a client object and calls the .query() method with a GraphQL query string. The query is named GetLocations and requests fields such as id, name, description, and photo. The result of the query is then logged to the console. A "Copy" button is visible in the top right corner of the code block.

The screenshot shows a window titled "gapcmn: UPS Information Panels {NS1.SKOONA.NET}" from the apcupsd software. The main content is a graph displaying historical data for an uninterruptible power supply (UPS). The graph plots various metrics over time, including LINEV (line voltage), LOADPCT (load percentage), TIMELEFT (time remaining), BCHARGE (battery charge), and BATTV (battery voltage). The status of the UPS at "house_services@ns1.skoona.net" is shown as "ONLINE". There are several buttons visible, including "Refresh" and "Close", and a message at the bottom indicates that automatic refresh has completed.

The screenshot displays a software application named "AraSuite," which appears to be an educational tool for children. The main window shows a grid of cells, each containing a simple image such as fruits or vegetables. A dialog box titled "Búsqueda de Imágenes" (Image Search) is open in the foreground. This dialog allows users to search for images by entering keywords in a text field. Below the search bar, a list of 21 matching images is displayed, including illustrations of a tree, a fruit stand, a woman with produce, and various fruits like bananas and apples. The interface includes buttons labeled "Buscar" (Search), "Insertar" (Insert), and "Cancelar" (Cancel). The overall design suggests it's used for creating interactive exercises involving images.

The screenshot shows the APNG Assembler application window on a macOS system. The main interface is divided into several sections. On the left, there is a list of image files with their names, sizes, and delays, which are used to create an animated PNG. The list includes "frame01.png" through "frame06.png", each with a size of 0 KB or 1 KB and a delay of 1/10 second. The "Assembly" tab is selected, indicating the user is in the process of creating an animation. Below the file list, there are options for playback settings, such as "Play indefinitely" and "Skip the first frame". The compression section offers three options: zlib, 7zip, and Zopfli, with 7zip currently selected. In the "Optimizations" section, checkboxes for "Palette" and "Color type" are checked. There are also fields for setting the "All frames delay" and "Selected frames delay", both set to 1/10 seconds. At the bottom of the window, there is a text field showing the output path for the generated APNG file, which is "/Users/maxst/Desktop/output.png", and a "Start" button to begin the assembly process.

The screenshot displays a desktop environment with a terminal window titled "Alacritty" open on the left side. The terminal prompt shows "gblive@greenbang ~]$". On the right side of the screen, there is a menu overlay for "GreenBANG", which lists various options including Terminal, Browser, File Manager, Editor, and Install. This menu also provides keyboard shortcuts for these functions and other Openbox controls. The desktop background features a scenic image of mountains and trees. At the bottom of the screen, a taskbar or dock is visible with several icons.

The screenshot shows a web page for the "Arclight" project, which is described as a "Bukkit server implementation on common mod loaders." The main content area features a table with information about different versions of the software, including "Release," "Forge," "NeoForge," "Fabric," "Status," and "Downloads." The current status for all listed versions is "ACTIVE." Below this table, there is a section titled "Legacy versions" with a "Details" link. A large image in the center displays a logo with the letters "ARC" inside a crescent moon shape. At the bottom of the screen, there is an "Installing" section with instructions to download a JAR file and launch it with a specific command.

The screenshot shows the Arduino IDE (Integrated Development Environment) with a sketch open. The code in the editor is written in C++ and is for an Arduino board, as indicated by the function names like 'pinMode' and 'digitalWrite'. The code includes comments explaining the setup and loop functions. The output console at the bottom of the window displays a message indicating that the "Compilation complete." The title bar shows the application name "Arduino IDE" and the current sketch name "Blink". The status bar at the bottom indicates that the Arduino Uno is not connected.

The screenshot displays the Areca Backup application interface. The window is divided into several sections: a navigation pane on the left showing a hierarchical folder structure; a central pane listing files and directories with details like name, size, and date; and a right-hand panel displaying file history and modification dates. At the top of the central pane, tabs such as "Archives," "Logical view," "History," "Indicators," "Search," "Log," and "Progression" are visible. The bottom section shows metadata about the selected item, including fields for Item, Local ID, Unique ID, Description, Source, Directory, and Type.

The screenshot shows the Argos Translate application with two main windows open. The top window, titled "Argos Translate," displays a simple interface for translation. It has dropdown menus to select the source and target languages, set as English and Spanish respectively. Below these are text boxes showing "Hello World!" in English and its translated version "¡Hola Mundo!" in Spanish. The bottom window is a terminal-like interface displaying command-line output related to package management. It lists various packages with columns for name, version, language code, and options to uninstall. The dock at the bottom of the screen shows several application icons.

The screenshot shows the Ares Galaxy file-sharing application. The main window is titled "Ares 2.1.7.3041 [Control Panel]" and indicates the user is online with a connection status of "connected as blabla, sharing 401 files". The interface features a menu bar with tabs for Library, Screen, Search, Transfer, Chat, and Control Panel. The "Control Panel" tab is active, displaying several sub-tabs including General, Transfer, Chat, Network, Hashlinks, Skin, BitTorrent, and Filesharing. On the left side, there is a list of skins such as Bloody, Borrovinio, and Esmaralda, with "General" selected. The right panel displays information about the "Base Skin", including its author, version, date, URL, and details. At the bottom, a media player-like control bar is visible.

The screenshot shows the user interface of a digital audio workstation (DAW) called "Aria Maestosa". The main area displays a music project with multiple tracks. The top track, labeled "Lead", is a standard staff for musical notation, showing a melody in 4/4 time. Below it, a second track, labeled "Nylon String Guitar", shows a guitar tablature. A third track at the bottom, labeled "Drums", presents a drum track with various percussion symbols. The software has a menu bar with options like File, Edit, and Help, and a toolbar with transport controls (Play, Stop, etc.) and other settings. The title of the project is "Untitled".

The screenshot displays the game "Armagetron Advanced," a 3D light cycle racing game. The gameplay is viewed from a third-person perspective, showing a futuristic arena with a grid-like floor and glowing walls. The player's character is represented by a small white triangle in the center of the screen. Other players are indicated by blue rectangular shapes on the track. The interface includes various text elements: at the top left, it shows that the user is watching four other players ("Dockatee," "Hawk," "Ex1y7," "Luzifer"). At the bottom left, there is a scoreboard showing the player's rank ("Me: Top"), score ("0"), and speed ("Fastest: Potato Chef (49.6)"). At the bottom right, information about enemies and friends is displayed. The top right corner shows the current time ("05:51 PM") and frames per second ("59 FPS").

The screenshot shows a terminal window with a dark background and light text. The content displayed is the help output for a command-line tool named "asar". The text includes the usage syntax, a list of available commands such as 'pack', 'list', 'extract-file', and 'extract', along with their descriptions. It also lists two options: '-h, --help' to output usage information and '-V, --version' to output the version number. The cursor is not visible, and the window appears to be in a static state.

The screenshot shows the login screen for the application "ArmCord" on a Fedora operating system. The main content is a dark, rounded rectangular dialog box with a "Welcome back!" message. It contains fields for "EMAIL OR PHONE NUMBER" and "PASSWORD", a "Forgot your password?" link, and a blue "Log in" button. To the right of these fields, there is an option to "Log in with QR Code". The background of the window features a colorful, abstract illustration with characters. The top bar of the screen shows the time as 10:39 and the date as Tuesday, December 20. The desktop environment appears to be GNOME.

The screenshot displays the interface of "Ascii Generator 2", a software application used to convert images into ASCII art. The main window shows a grayscale image of a person's face rendered in ASCII characters. Various controls are visible, including options for size, font, and character sets. A print preview window is open, showing the generated ASCII art. On the left side, there is a panel with text parameters like "Size", "Font", and "Ramp". At the bottom, a histogram and a small preview of the original image are shown.

The screenshot displays the web-based administration interface for an Asus router running the Asuswrt-Merlin firmware. The interface has a dark theme with a sidebar menu on the left listing various configuration options such as "Quick Internet Setup," "Network Map," "Wireless," and "Advanced Settings." The main content area shows system status information, including network connectivity details (e.g., WAN IP), wireless security settings ("WPAP2-Personal"), CPU usage, RAM usage, and client connections. There are also graphs showing CPU and RAM utilization.

The screenshot shows a command-line interface window, specifically the Windows Command Prompt. The application running is "Artistic Style" (AStyle) version 2.04, as indicated at the top of the console. The program has processed a directory of C++ source files located in `..\AStyle\src\*.cpp` and header files in `..\AStyle\src\*.h`. The output lists which files were changed (formatted) and which were left unchanged. A summary at the bottom indicates that 3 files were formatted, 6 were unchanged, the process took 0.47 seconds, and 17,332 lines were processed. The prompt at the bottom asks the user to "Press any key to continue...".

The screenshot shows a web-based interface for Trixbox, an open platform for business telephony. The main page is titled "trixbox CE" and displays system status information. On the left, a navigation menu includes options like System Status, Packages, Asterisk, and Settings. The central part of the screen shows the "System Status" with a list of services such as Asterisk, web server, cron server, SSH server, and MySQL, all marked as "running" except for the "Hud Server" which is "N/A". There are also sections for Network Usage, Memory Usage, and Mounted Filesystems, each showing various statistics. The top right corner shows the server time, login, and register buttons.
